papers.title: A singularity detecting uniformly convergent quantum wavelet framework for weakly singular nonlocal Emden--Fowler systems with quantum Mittag--Leffler sources
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum wavelet-based computational framework for coupled systems of Caputo-type quantum ($q$-) fractional Emden--Fowler problems with $q$-Mittag--Leffler source terms, where the solutions exhibit singular behavior in time. Here $q\in(0,1)$ denotes the parameter of $q$-calculus. The highest-order Caputo $q$-fractional derivatives are expanded through the Haar wavelet basis, and the lower-order fractional derivatives are approximated through Jackson $q$-fractional integrals of Haar wavelets. The continuous problem reduces to a nonlinear algebraic system on the midpoint collocation points. Under suitable structural assumptions, the Banach fixed-point theorem yields the existence and uniqueness of the continuous solutions and wellposedness of the discrete solutions on collocation points. The nonlinearity of the given problem is dealt with by the damped Newton's iteration. In addition, We prove stability of the scheme and derive rigorous convergence estimates in a weighted norm that remains uniformly controlled despite the appearance of singular weight at $t=0$ in the continuous model. When the highest-order fractional derivatives are H\"older continuous with exponent $\sigma$, the mathematical error of weakly singular solution and its lower-order fractional derivatives become $\mathcal{O}(\tau_L^{\sigma})$, where $\tau_L=2^{-(L+1)}$ denotes the width of the finest subintervals for maximum level of resolution $L$. First-order convergence is guaranteed under stronger regularity with $\sigma=1$. Several test cases are considered to confirm the accuracy and robustness of the present approach, which strongly agrees with the theoretical estimates. In particular, first-order convergence is observed even where the stronger regularity assumption is not satisfied.

papers.title: Moser--Trudinger inequalities and the complex Monge--Amp\`ere mean field equation
papers.abstract: We study sharp Moser--Trudinger inequalities for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere energy. On the unit ball, we determine the optimal energy coefficient and additive constant in the logarithmic Moser--Trudinger inequality. We deduce subcritical Moser--Trudinger inequalities in exponential form with explicit bounds proportional to $\varepsilon^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the relative distance to the critical coefficient. The proof establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness for the associated mean field equation by showing that every smooth solution has constant boundary normal derivative. This gives existence and uniqueness precisely for total masses $0<\Lambda<[2\pi(n+1)]^n$, proving Berman--Berndtsson's conjecture. We also establish smoothness of bounded pluripotential and finite-energy solutions. Domain monotonicity transfers the exponential estimates and the optimal logarithmic energy coefficient to bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains.

papers.title: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Amp\`ere equations in big classes
papers.abstract: We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact K\"ahler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,\alpha}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.

papers.title: The Sharp Holder Constant in Mori's Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $K\ge 1$ and let $f$ be a $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ onto itself with $f(0)=0$. We prove that $\lvert f(a)-f(b)\rvert\le 16^{1-\frac{1}{K}}\lvert a-b\rvert^{\frac{1}{K}}$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb{D}$. The constant is sharp, confirming the conjectured value of the Mori constant. The proof reduces the estimate along a Beltrami path to an infinitesimal inequality, which follows from quasiconformal distortion bounds and a three-pole integral estimate.

papers.title: Real-Rootedness and Log-Concavity of Zigzag Eulerian Polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove that the zigzag Eulerian polynomials have only real, negative, simple zeros, and hence strictly log-concave coefficients, settling the first two parts of a conjecture of Petersen and Zhuang. Real-rootedness in combinatorics is usually proved inside a single algebraic framework, such as interlacing or stability. Our proof rests on a different premise: different parts of a zero set become visible in different representations of the same polynomial, and classical tools suffice once each part is viewed in the right one. The bridge between representations is a local rule. Forgetting the order in which a bounded-jump path visits positions leaves only a nearest-neighbor condition on sorted gaps, which makes an encoding via a transfer matrix much simpler to see. From there the argument passes to complex analysis. The sizes of the matrix's eigenmodes locate the zeros at the two ends of the negative axis, through Rouch\'e's theorem. In a logarithmic coordinate the generating function becomes a combination of derivatives of the hyperbolic secant, akin to the classical derivative polynomials, and the arguments of its nearest poles produce a sine that fixes the signs between consecutive central zeros. The zeros are thus read off from the poles of an associated kernel. More broadly, the proof suggests that combinatorial polynomials defined by local constraints carry analytic structure, in their spectra and in the poles of their kernels, that is complementary to the usual algebraic methods and that classical complex analysis can exploit directly.

papers.title: $\mathrm{BMOA}$ and Carleson-homogeneous Denjoy domains
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a proper closed subset of the extended real line that contains $[-\infty,-1]\cup[1,+\infty]$, and let $F$ be a universal covering of the Denjoy domain $\Omega=\overline{\mathbb C}\setminus E$. We prove the conjecture of Huo and Zinsmeister that $E$ is Carleson-homogeneous if $\log F'\in\mathrm{BMOA}(\mathbb D)$. The proof is based on an estimate for the length of $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ in terms of the Bloch seminorm of $\log F'$ and a weighted $L^2$ integral of $F''/F'$. From this estimate we deduce that $\Omega$ has the Hayman-Wu property, and Carleson-homogeneity then follows from a theorem of Fern\'andez. We also characterize these domains by Carleson measure conditions for the arclength on $F^{-1}(\mathbb R)$ and for the Schwarzian derivative of $F$, and by the $H^\infty$ interpolation property of the inverse images of suitable sequences in ${\mathbb R}\setminus E$.

papers.title: Lectures on Bergman Theory (The first part)
papers.abstract: The first half of these lecture notes provides a systematic introduction to the Bergman theory on domains, as well as parameter dependence of weighted Bergman Kernels. Starting from the Bergman space, it establishes the reproducing property, extremal characterizations and transformation laws of the Bergman kernel, and discusses removable singularities, stability, and boundary growth, which also includes a nice Bergman kernel proof of Riemann's mapping theorem. It then studies the completeness and curvature properties of the Bergman metric, including Kobayashi' criterion and Lu Qi-Keng's ball theorem. Finally, it explores the parameter continuity, regularity, plurisubharmonicity, and convexity of weighted Bergman Kernels, which found significant applications in the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities.

papers.title: A Burns-Krantz theorem on convex domains
papers.abstract: We prove two boundary rigidity theorems for holomorphic self-maps of bounded convex domains. Let $\Omega\subset\C^n$, $n\geq1$, and suppose that $\partial\Omega$ is $C^{1,\alpha}$ near $p\in\partial\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\leq1$. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ satisfies $f(z)=z+o(|z-p|^3)$ as $z\to p$ in one fixed non-tangential approach region at $p$, then $f=\id_\Omega$. We also prove a rigidity theorem for bounded convex domains $\Omega$ without assuming boundary smoothness. If a holomorphic self-map $f$ of $\Omega$ satisfies $f(z)-z=O(|z-p|^m)$ as $z\to p\in\partial\Omega$ for some $m>1+2\pi/\theta_p$, where $\theta_p$ is the supremum of sector angles in the open tangent cone at $p$, taken over complex lines through its vertex, then $f=\id_\Omega$, which proves a conjecture of Zimmer.

papers.title: A Quasiconformal Squeezing function and Fridman invariant and applications
papers.abstract: The squeezing function and Fridman invariant are two examples of biholomorphic invariants that have proved to be useful in exploring questions in complex geometry. Motivated by their construction, we define conformal analogues of these invariants by using suitable families of $K$-quasiconformal mappings, and study several basic properties such as continuity, domain dependence and boundary behaviour near spherically extreme points. It is also shown that these conformal invariants are explicitly related. As an application, we propose and prove variants of the Ferrand--Obata theorem in conformal geometry that apply to domains in $\mbb R^n$. This highlights the close analogy that exists between the Ferrand--Obata and Wong--Rosay theorems.

papers.title: The Koebe radius for univalent cubics
papers.abstract: Let \(p(z)=z+a_2z^2+a_3z^3\) be a polynomial univalent in the unit disk \(\Delta\). We determine the largest disk centered at the origin that is contained in the image \(p(\Delta)\) of every such polynomial. Its squared radius is the unique real root of \[ 27q^3-54q^2+63q-8=0. \] We also find the extremal polynomial \(p_*\).

papers.title: Higher-Derivative Conjectures of Sendov
papers.abstract: We prove Conjectures~3 and~8 of Sendov's 2002 survey and deduce Conjecture~9. More precisely, let $p$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. For every integer $s$ with $1\le s<n$, we prove that each zero of $p$ lies within distance $2s/(s+1)$ of a zero of $p^{(s)}$. For quartics, we obtain the sharp bound $2/\sqrt3$ for the second derivative and determine all polynomials attaining it.

papers.title: Circle packing and Riemann uniformization of random planar maps in an ergodic scale-free environment
papers.abstract: We prove that embedded infinite planar maps in ergodic scale-free environments are close to their circle packing and Riemann uniformization embeddings on a large scale, as long as suitable moment and connectivity conditions are satisfied. In subsequent work we use these results to prove convergence of random planar maps to Liouville quantum gravity under circle packing and Riemann uniformization embeddings.

papers.title: Annihilating ideals and Agler--McCarthy spectral varieties in the bidisc
papers.abstract: The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.

papers.title: Strictly paired ${\rm CR}$ linear automorphisms of $\R^4$
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the algebraic and differential geometric properties of smooth mappings between domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$, classifying them according to the constant ranks of their holomorphic and antiholomorphic derivative components. Particular emphasis is placed on strictly paired CR (SPCR) linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$, where both block matrices $A$ and $B$ have rank 1. We characterise the set of SPCR linear automorphisms as a 12-dimensional submanifold of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{C})^2$ and analyse its underlying CR structure, demonstrating its geometric and structural rigidity.

papers.title: The Dimension Conjecture for Hypersurfaces Is True
papers.abstract: The dimension conjecture in CR geometry is proved for arbitrary real-analytic hypersurfaces. More precisely, for $N\ge2$ the dimension of the Lie algebra of infinitesimal holomorphic automorphisms of a germ of a holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^N$ of the indicated class does not exceed $N^2+2N$. This is exactly the dimension of the corresponding algebra for any Levi-nondegenerate hyperquadric in the same ambient space. Equality holds if and only if the germ is equivalent to a hyperquadric. For a finitely nondegenerate hypersurface with constant positive Levi rank $r$ satisfying $0<r<N-1$, the sharper bound $N^2+r+1=N^2+N-m$ is obtained, where $m=N-1-r$. We also establish the sharper bound $N^2+N-1$ for the automorphism algebra of a nonspherical holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface; consequently, dimensions $N^2+N,...,N^2+2N-1$ cannot occur (a dimension gap).

papers.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
papers.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d\ge 2$ with $p(0)=0$ and $p'(0)\ne 0$, let $S(p)$ be the minimum of $|p(c)/(c\,p'(0))|$ over the critical points $c$ of $p$, and let $K(d)$ be the supremum of $S(p)$ over all such $p$ of degree $d$. In 1981 Smale proved that $K(d)\le 4$ for every $d$, and asked whether $4$ can be replaced by $1$. We prove that Smale's mean value constant $\sup_dK(d)$ equals $4$ and that $K(d)\to4$ as $d\to\infty$, combining a reduction due to Jatar and Ng with an explicit construction. Each $K(d)$ is known to be below $4$, so the supremum is not attained. The main result has also been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $\xi$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $\zeta$ of $p$ such that $ |\xi-\zeta|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.The Lean 4 formalization of the main results are also provided.
